official_sources: Land affected by contamination planning guidance
Voluntary remediation advice contaminated land and groundwater 2026

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning suitability role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning guidance requires contamination implications to be addressed so land is suitable for its proposed new use and unacceptable pollution risk is prevented, while recognising separate regulatory regimes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Source pathway receptor model
official_measurement_examples.fact: Where contamination may be an issue, planning guidance expects a proportionate risk assessment identifying potential sources, pathways and receptors and evaluating pollutant linkages.

official_measurement_examples.name: LCRM risk-based sequence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency LCRM uses a risk-based process to identify contamination, assess receptor risk, appraise remediation options, carry out remediation and verify effectiveness.

official_measurement_examples.name: Part 2A legal threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: Part 2A statutory guidance states land should not be treated as legally contaminated land unless unacceptable risks are clearly identified through the required risk assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning and Part 2A separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance treats planning redevelopment and Part 2A as different routes; Part 2A is intended for cases where no appropriate alternative solution exists.

official_measurement_examples.name: Groundwater remedial targets
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency groundwater guidance requires remedial targets and compliance points to protect groundwater and defined receptors where historic contamination creates unacceptable risk.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 voluntary advice limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Environment Agency voluntary remediation advice service published 3 June 2026 is advisory for controlled-water contamination and explicitly cannot confirm that future planning or permit submissions will be acceptable.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permission separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Contamination investigation, remediation verification, planning conditions, environmental permits, waste controls and Part 2A determinations are separate controls and none alone establishes parcel development capacity or ownership.

core_rules: presence of a contaminant is not automatically a Part 2A contaminated-land determination
historic industrial use is a risk indicator not proof of unacceptable current risk
a desk study is not remediation verification
a conceptual site model is not planning permission
planning permission is not proof contamination has been remediated
Part 2A determination is distinct from planning redevelopment controls
LCRM Stage 1 evidence must not be represented as completed remediation
LCRM Stage 2 options appraisal is not verification of remedial success
LCRM Stage 3 verification must retain actual evidence and dates
groundwater compliance targets are receptor-specific not universal soil clearance levels
voluntary Environment Agency advice is advisory and not future planning approval
waste classification and environmental permitting are distinct from planning permission
historic remediation reports must retain scope date contaminants and verification limitations
contamination compliance does not determine ownership access rights or utility capacity
no parcel contamination clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK, Defra and Environment Agency sources were checked on 2026-07-26. The June 2026 voluntary remediation service and LCRM/Part 2A distinctions were preserved; no parcel remediation or development conclusion was promoted.
